text: py/iris_kmeans.py (small, seeded computation iris): R/iris_pre.R: pre-script builds to_py, gets target’s reproducible seed straight targets: R/iris_post.R: post-script reads variables back. tarpolyglot binds py (reticulate __main__ proxy) py_get(name) (explicit reticulate::py_to_r() shortcut). last expression target’s value: _targets.R: need read one variables verbatim (reshaping), drop post-script use retrieve instead: py_get() lookup :
code: import numpy as np  # `df` (a pandas DataFrame) and `seed` (an int) were pushed from R. rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) X = df[["Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"]].to_numpy()  # pick 3 random initial centres, reproducibly (same seed -> same pick) idx = rng.choice(X.shape[0], size=3, replace=False) result = {"n": int(X.shape[0]), "centers": X[idx].tolist()} # `df` is bound from inputs = c(df = "iris_data"). # tar_seed_get() returns THIS target's deterministic seed (derived from the # pipeline seed and the target name), so the Python RNG is reproducible. to_py <- list(   df   = df,   seed = targets::tar_seed_get() ) res <- py_get("result")               # or: res <- py$result data.frame(n = res$n, k = length(res$centers)) library(targets) library(tarpolyglot)  list(   tar_target(iris_data, iris),    tar_target_py(     name = km,     script = "py/iris_kmeans.py",     inputs = c(df = "iris_data"),     pre_script = "R/iris_pre.R",     post_script = "R/iris_post.R"       # returns a data.frame into the pipeline   ) ) tar_target_py(   name = km,   script = "py/iris_kmeans.py",   inputs = c(df = "iris_data"),   pre_script = "R/iris_pre.R",   retrieve = "result"                   # returns the Python `result` as an R list )

text: limitation 1 (one interpreter per session), clean way give step fresh interpreter, let different steps use different environments, run separate worker processes crew. tarpolyglot ships controller preconfigured : polyglot_controller() wraps crew::crew_controller_local() tasks_max = 1L: worker runs one task retires, every foreign step starts brand-new interpreter. controller set, tarpolyglot targets (whose deployment defaults "worker") run workers automatically. Foreign steps workers, ordinary R steps main process. common setup: heavy R work stays -process, Python/Julia/Rust steps go controller. Flip global default deployment = "main" override just foreign steps back "worker": per-step deployment = "worker" required : without Python step also inherit "main" run -process, interpreter isolation. Foreign R steps different workers. Use named crew::crew_controller_group() route target controller name; set R controller default via resources ordinary targets need extra argument: Dynamic branching works unchanged: inputs become real dependencies, pattern branches , crew spreads branches across workers (fresh interpreter tasks_max = 1): See vignette("python"), vignette("julia"), vignette("rust") full per-language reference, ?polyglot_controller controller options.
code: tar_option_set(controller = polyglot_controller(workers = 2L)) tar_option_set(   controller = polyglot_controller(workers = 1L),   deployment = "main"                    # every ordinary tar_target() stays on main )  list(   tar_target(iris_data, iris),           # main process   tar_target_py(     name = km,     script = "py/iris_kmeans.py",     inputs = c(df = "iris_data"),     pre_script = "R/iris_pre.R",     retrieve = "result",     deployment = "worker"                # THIS step runs on the polyglot worker   ) ) tar_option_set(   controller = crew::crew_controller_group(     polyglot_controller(name = "poly", workers = 2L),          # Python/Julia/Rust     crew::crew_controller_local(name = "rmain", workers = 4L)  # ordinary R targets   ),   resources = tar_resources(crew = tar_resources_crew(controller = "rmain")) )  list(   tar_target(iris_data, iris),           # -> "rmain" (the default)   tar_target_py(     name = km,     script = "py/iris_kmeans.py",     inputs = c(df = "iris_data"),     pre_script = "R/iris_pre.R",     retrieve = "result",     resources = tar_resources(crew = tar_resources_crew(controller = "poly"))   ) ) list(   tar_target(iris_groups, split(iris, iris$Species), iteration = "list"),  # 3 groups   tar_target_py(     name = per_species,     script = "py/iris_kmeans.py",     inputs = c(df = "iris_groups"),     pre_script = "R/iris_pre.R",     retrieve = "result",     pattern = map(iris_groups),          # one branch per species, in parallel     iteration = "list"   ) )

Rust step pre-script: #[extendr] functions compiled called R post-script. Output returned either converted R object character vector files disk (output = "file").
